6791E Reminders

6791E Example

DHS-6791E Reminders

Case Managers should review the Reassessment timeline and send the DHS-6791E referral between the 120th and 150th day from the end of the Service Agreement.

For example, if the Service Agreement ends 4/30/26, the referral must be submitted between 12/1/26 and 1/20/27. If a referral is sent after 1/20/27, it is considered late and is at risk of a gap in service due to delayed assignment to a MnCHOICES Certified Assessor.

What should be included on the DHS-6791E?

  • Date Form Sent to County of Residence
  • Type of Assessment
    • Early Reassessment: Please include the reason for the request and detailed information about any health changes.
    • 65th Birthday: Please include the 65th Birthday Checklist (DHS-8691) form with the request. If you have already submitted the referral and the person no longer is requesting a 65th birthday assessment, please email RA Intake
  • Documents Attached
    • DD Waiver or Rule 185 Reassessment: Please include the Rule 185 Eligibility Form to confirm the person continues to meet eligibility for Rule 185 Case Management with an appropriate ICD-10 codes. Children ages 5 and older must receive updated testing and have a valid ICD-10 code.
  • Current Program
  • Details & Information
    • Correct demographic information related to the person (beware of using another person’s information)
  • Guardian
  • Contact for Scheduling
  • Case Manager
    • Operated staff should include the appropriate unit case aide email address
    • Case Managers should include their NPI number so that the Assessor can enter the administrative activity LTC SD to the assigned Case Manager
  • Assessment/Communication Tips and Advice/Supporting Information
    • Please enter any information that will be helpful to the Assessor

DHS-6791E Email Naming Convention

Ramsey County Reassessment Intake receives and reviews an extremely high volume of referrals every month for a variety of programs. Case Managers should submit their referrals using the appropriate email naming convention to assist with coordinating cases for distribution. Please see the examples.

  Last Name, First Name, PMI, Type of Assessment, SA End Date OR Submission
Annual RA

Brown, Charlie, PMI# 01234567, Annual 12.31.26

Rule 185/DD Waiver should include the Rule 185 Eligibility Form.CAC Reassessments should include the DHS-7096.
Early RA

Brown, Charlie, PMI# 01234567, Early RA 09.03.26 (Date of submission)

Case Manager should include detailed information regarding the request for an early reassessment.
65th Birthday

Brown, Charlie, PMI# 01234567, 65th BDay 09.03.26

DHS changed the process for 65th Birthday Assessment as of 8/1/26. Please refer to the 65th BD Process 09.01.2026.
Rule 185/DD CM

Brown, Charlie, PMI# 01234567, Annual 12.31.26 (Date is the month after assessment was completed)

Individuals with Rule 185 CM Only have the right to waive their annual reassessment. Individuals who utilize CFSS/PCA/CSG or are living in an ICF-DD cannot waive their annual assessment.

 

Rule 185 and Developmental Disability Review

When the MnCHOICES QDDP assessors find a person eligible for R185 the case goes to Middle Ground who then assigns it to a Case Manager.

The assessor attaches important documents in MnCHOICES. These include the following:

  1. Eligibility Determination Form
  2. Psychological Determinations
  3. Medical Information
  4. DHS-7209
  5. IEPs

These documents are important and need to be saved in your agency “permanent” file as they are part of documenting eligibility.

Eligibility Determination Form

  • This is also known as the Rule 185 Developmental Disability/Related Condition Eligibility Determination. This form includes the following:
  • Why the person is eligible (there will be scores for both IQ and Adaptive Functioning)
  • When the testing was completed and by whom
  • When new testing is needed (this is especially important for cases that were assessed before the age of 5 as they will need new testing after they turn 5 years old)

Psychological Information

  • This could be from a clinic, hospital or even a school evaluation
  • Often includes the diagnosis and ICD-10 codes (school evaluations do not include the codes)
  • Include good information on cognitive and adaptive functioning

Medical Information

  • May include a ICD-10 code that is needed
  • Often include secondary conditions related to the main diagnosis

DHS-7209

  • Also known as the DD Waiver Waiting List Category Determination Tool
  • If they are not on a waiver this will guide you on whether you begin the process for a waiver
  • The assessor/reassessor completes to indicate the level of need for a waiver
  • Institutional Exit: Is leaving a NF or ICF (Immediate Need)
  • Immediate Need: Unstable housing, loss of caregiver, abusive environment and sudden change in need. The assessor will have begun the financial paperwork for MA-LTC or will work with the Case Manager on this
  • Defined Need: Does the person have an assessed need for a waiver within one-year of the assessment. The Case Manager will work with the person/family on getting the MA-LTC to open the waiver
  • Future Need: Does not have a current need or does not want to start waiver services at this time

IEPs

  • IEP’s provide information on how the they works with the person
  • Can provide information on current functioning
  • May provide additional information on what approaches and strategies work

AC Overdue Fees: Case Manager Responsibilities and Resources

This information is specific to Case Managers (CMs) who support people enrolled in the Alternative Care (AC) program.

Understanding the importance of AC fees and knowing where to find additional resources can help Case Managers appropriately follow up with people who have overdue fees.

What Are AC Overdue Fee Reports?

The AC Overdue Fee Report is a monthly report that identifies people with overdue AC fees. The report is organized by county of service and assigned Case Manager. The Minnesota Department of Human Services (DHS) updates the report every two weeks.

DHS does not send the report directly to people enrolled in the AC program. Instead, the report is sent by email to the lead agency and is provided to the Case Manager assigned to the case in MMIS.

It is the lead agency’s responsibility to ensure the report is provided to the appropriate Case Manager. Case Managers are responsible for following up with each person listed on the report.

During follow-up, the Case Manager should discuss the person’s overdue fees and remind them that they are responsible for paying the full AC fee amount each month, even if they are making partial payments.

AC Fees and Estate Recovery

The total amount of outstanding overdue fees and the cost of AC services may be claimed by the state or DHS through estate recovery.

Lead agencies should share the following resources with people enrolled in the AC program:

  • AC Program Recovery Information, DHS-5186 (PDF)
  • AC Program Monthly Fee and Payment Information, DHS-4639 (PDF)

Understanding Payments and the Overdue Fee Report

When a person makes a payment and has overdue fees, the payment is applied to their oldest overdue balance.

If the balance is not changing and there are no new additional charges, the Case Manager should consider whether the person is still enrolled in AC.

People may continue to appear on the report after they are no longer enrolled in AC. Individuals remain on the report until after their death and until estate recovery has reviewed their file. As a result, a person may continue to appear on the report for years even though they are no longer enrolled in AC.

If a Case Manager has a person on their report who is no longer enrolled in AC, no additional follow-up is needed.

Case Managers with questions about AC overdue fees or related processes can contact DHS at:

Dhs.aasd.hcbs@state.mn.us 

Reminder: Extended PCA Service Lines Ending September 30, 2026

Please be aware that all extended PCA service lines, regardless of waiver type, must end on September 30, 2026.

This includes the following codes:

  • T1019 UC
  • T1019 TT UC
  • T1019 HQ UC
  • T1019 TG UC
  • T1019 TG TT UC
  • T1019 HQ TG UC

DHS Extended PCA Information

Case Managers should plan accordingly. The expectation is that CFSS will be used in place of extended PCA when appropriate.

You may also notice that some extended PCA SA lines have already been ended effective September 30, 2026. Ramsey County is taking this preemptive step to ensure compliance with the requirement. As a result, some SA lines will be addressed behind the scenes and may not require action from the Case Manager.

Understanding “Customization” on the 6790

It is important for Case Managers (CMs) to understand what “customization” means on a 6790 and how selecting this option may impact the rate.

When the customization box is checked on a 6790, two criteria must be met:

  1. The person must have a specific assessment score on their MN-CHOICE assessment.
    Case Managers should review the person’s DD or LTC screening document to determine whether the required criteria are met.

    Quick reference guide on deaf/hard of hearing customization in the RMS

  2. Staff providing the service must be fluent signers of sign language.
    The staff members must use this skill to provide services to a person who meets the criteria identified in the screening document.

Important Reminder

If a person receiving waiver services does not meet both of these criteria, the customization box should not be checked on the 6790.

Support Plan Updates

Selecting the assessment to correspond to the support plan

What’s changing?

  • When creating a new support plan or revising an Initial or annual/reassessment support plan, a user must select an assessment with a complete status (Completed – Ready for MMIS, Pending MMIS response or Approved by MMIS) to link it to a specific support plan.
  • When a support plan is in the “In Progress status,” a new Assessment Form field is available in the Overview section under the About Plan subsection.
  • This field displays a drop-down list of the person's completed assessments and users must select the appropriate assessment to link to the support plan.
  • A new Assessment form field will be available in the Overview section, under the About plan subsection, while the support plan is in the In progress status.
  • Note: If a user linked the wrong assessment after the support plan goes past the “In progress status”, they must discard the support plan and create a new one with the correct assessment linked to it.
  • When a support plan is revised using the reason “Plan revision,” the originally linked assessment stays linked to the revised plan and cannot be changed.
  • This enhancement does not apply to support plans with the reason “Transition plan” because those plans are not associated with an assessment.

The information in this section is directly from DHS

Contacting CMS

If you have concerns regarding a policy, decision, or guidance issued by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), you may contact CMS directly to share your feedback.

When contacting CMS, it is helpful to include the following information:

  • Your name, organization, and contact information.
  • The specific CMS policy, guidance, or decision you are commenting on.
  • A clear description of your concerns.
  • Examples of how the decision impacts individuals, providers, counties, or other stakeholders.
  • Any supporting information or data you would like CMS to consider.
  • The outcome or action you are requesting from CMS.

Contact the regional office:

  • General phone: (312) 353-9866
  • General regional email: ROCHIORA@cms.hhs.gov
  • General CMS Region 5 contact page: CMS Chicago Regional Office
  • CMS Regional Offices directory: CMS Regional Offices

For concerns related to Medicaid or Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) waivers: Contact CMS Region 5 (Chicago Regional Office), which serves Minnesota through its Division of Medicaid and Children's Health.

  • Phone: (312) 353-3653
  • Email: ROCHIORA@cms.hhs.gov

Please note that the Minnesota Department of Human Services cannot modify or overturn Federal Regulations, CMS policy or guidance. Stakeholders who wish to provide feedback regarding CMS decisions are encouraged to contact CMS directly using the information above.

Reporting Contacts

If a case manager has concerns with services not being delivered in the manner that is outlined in the persons support plan or in accordance with waiver policy then the following is recommended:

  • Report concerns to the provider's licensing agency or to DHS Licensing Divisions Central Intake at (651) 431-6600,
  • MAARC reporting for suspected abuse of vulnerable adults:
    • By Phone (for general public and mandated reporters) 1-844-880-1574
    • Online (for mandated reporters only) Link to report
  • If the provider is billing for services not provided make a report to The Program Integrity and Oversight Division at DHS
